subs.label: Fantasy & Isekai Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by where the fantastic lies relative to our world: other worlds entered from ours, invented secondary worlds, myth, then the supernatural inside the modern world

leaves.label: Isekai (Transported to Another World)
leaves.defn: A series or film whose protagonist is physically carried, summoned or dropped from our world into another, and whose story turns on being an outsider there (Fushigi Yuugi, Re:Zero, Tate no Yuusha no Nariagari, Gate). Rebirth into the other world goes to C3-2; being trapped inside a game goes to C3-4.
leaves.aliases: isekai, isekai tenni, portal fantasy, reverse isekai
leaves.see: C3-2 Isekai Tensei; C3-4 Game-World Isekai; C3-3 Otome Isekai
leaves.axis: by how the hero crosses and what he does there: classic portal journeys, summoned heroes, free adventurers, modern know-how, parody; reverse isekai last

leaves.label: Isekai Tensei (Reincarnation)
leaves.defn: A story whose protagonist dies in our world and is reborn, with memories intact, into a fantasy world, as a person or as something else (Mushoku Tensei, Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken, Kumo desu ga, Nani ka?, Isekai Nonbiri Nouka). Reborn into an otome game goes to C3-3.
leaves.aliases: tensei, isekai tensei, reincarnation isekai, slow life
leaves.see: C3-1 Isekai; C3-3 Otome Isekai
leaves.axis: by what the hero is reborn as and the pace of the second life: new human life, non-human body, slow life

leaves.label: Otome Isekai (Villainess)
leaves.defn: A story whose heroine (rarely a hero) is reborn or transported into the world of an otome game or romance novel, typically as its doomed villainess, and must rewrite the plot (Otome Game no Hametsu Flag shika Nai Akuyaku Reijou ni Tensei shiteshimatta, Akuyaku Reijou Level 99, Seijo no Maryoku wa Bannou desu). A villainess romance with no crossing goes to C5-9.
leaves.aliases: akuyaku reijō, villainess isekai, otome-game isekai
leaves.see: C3-2 Isekai Tensei; C5-9 Romantic Fantasy; C5-3 Reverse Harem

leaves.label: Game-World Isekai (VRMMO & LitRPG)
leaves.defn: A story set inside an online or video game, or a world run on its rules, where the hero is a player, trapped player or transported avatar (Sword Art Online, .hack//Sign, Log Horizon, Overlord, Shangri-La Frontier). A fantasy world with mere status screens stays in C3-1.
leaves.aliases: VRMMO, LitRPG, trapped in a game
leaves.see: C3-1 Isekai; C7 Sports & Game Anime
leaves.axis: by whether the players can log out: trapped in the game, transported into a game world, voluntary VR play

leaves.label: High Fantasy
leaves.defn: A story set wholly in an invented secondary world with its own history, kingdoms and magic, built around wars, courts, journeys or the craft of magic rather than a questing party (Arslan Senki, Kemono no Souja Erin, Kino no Tabi, Little Witch Academia). Party adventure goes to C3-6; grim violence to C3-8.
leaves.see: C3-6 Sword and Sorcery; C3-8 Dark Fantasy; C5-9 Romantic Fantasy
leaves.axis: by what the world-building serves: war, court, journey, magic craft, fable

leaves.label: Sword and Sorcery
leaves.defn: A fantasy-world adventure whose engine is a hero or party of swordsmen, mages and thieves questing, fighting monsters and delving dungeons (Lodoss-tou Senki, Sousou no Frieren, Dungeon ni Deai wo Motomeru no wa Machigatteiru Darou ka, Tales of Zestiria the X). Comic sword and sorcery goes to C3-7; grimdark to C3-8.
leaves.aliases: adventure fantasy, adventurer guild, tsuihō (party exile)
leaves.see: C3-5 High Fantasy; C3-7 Comic Fantasy; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by the adventuring frame: questing parties, dungeons and guilds, party-exile stories, video-game franchises last

leaves.label: Comic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A secondary-world fantasy whose primary engine is comedy and genre parody (Slayers, Dragon Half, Mairimashita! Iruma-kun). Isekai parody goes to C3-1 section 5.
leaves.see: C3-6 Sword and Sorcery; C10 Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Dark Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy whose world is defined by horror, cruelty and despair, with demons, monsters and graphic violence (Berserk, Claymore, Shingeki no Kyojin, Devilman: Crybaby, Made in Abyss). Pure horror without a fantasy world goes to C9.
leaves.see: C3-6 Sword and Sorcery; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by the source of the darkness: grimdark warriors, demonic transformation, siege by monsters, gothic and fairy-tale darkness

leaves.label: Science Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy whose world mixes magic with lost technology, steampunk machines or a post-apocalyptic future (Tenkuu no Shiro Laputa, Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children, Utawarerumono, Houseki no Kuni). Hard science fiction goes to C2.
leaves.see: C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime; C3-5 High Fantasy

leaves.label: Mythic Fiction
leaves.defn: A story built from myth and religion: gods, kami, demons and the afterlife acting in a world or limbo of their own (Mononoke Hime, Haibane Renmei, Angel Beats!, Campione!). Chinese gods-and-demons stories go to C3-11; yōkai to C3-13.
leaves.see: C3-11 Shenmo & Xianxia; C3-13 Yōkai
leaves.axis: by the mythology: Japanese gods and kami, gods and demons of world myth, afterlife and limbo

leaves.label: Shenmo & Xianxia
leaves.defn: A Chinese-tradition fantasy of gods, demons, immortals and spirit beasts, from the shenmo classics to cultivation (xianxia) and fox-spirit tales (Hakujaden, Nezha Zhi Mo Tong Jiang Shi, Huyao Xiao Hongniang, Fanren Xiu Xian Zhuan). Martial-arts combat-first wuxia goes to C1.
leaves.aliases: shenmo xiaoshuo, gods and demons fiction, xianxia, cultivation
leaves.see: C3-10 Mythic Fiction; C1 Action & Battle Anime

leaves.label: Urban Fantasy
leaves.defn: A story set in the contemporary everyday world where magic, monsters or a hidden supernatural society exist alongside ordinary life (Durarara!!, Kara no Kyoukai, Kyoukai no Kanata, Bakemonogatari). Japanese folklore spirits go to C3-13; ghost hunters to C3-14; vampires to C3-15.
leaves.aliases: contemporary fantasy, low fantasy, modern fantasy
leaves.see: C3-13 Yōkai; C3-14 Occult Detective Fiction; C3-15 Vampire Fiction; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by how the supernatural is organised: hidden mage societies, beings in the city, everyday magic and contemporary fantasy films, the Monogatari oddity cycle

leaves.label: Yōkai Fiction
leaves.defn: A story whose supernatural beings are the yōkai, kami and spirits of Japanese folklore, met by seers, children or guardians (Natsume Yuujinchou, Mushishi, Gegege no Kitarou, Sen to Chihiro no Kamikakushi). Yōkai romances go to C5-8.
leaves.see: C3-10 Mythic Fiction; C3-12 Urban Fantasy; C5-8 Paranormal Romance
leaves.axis: by the encounter: seer and spirit tales, yōkai comedy and everyday life, battles with and for yōkai, the spirit world as a place

leaves.label: Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.defn: A story whose protagonists investigate and exorcise ghosts, curses and demons as a profession or calling (Tokyo Babylon, Ga-Rei: Zero, Koukyuu no Karasu, Muhyo to Rouji). Battle-first exorcist shōnen goes to C1.
leaves.see: C3-12 Urban Fantasy; C9 Horror Anime

leaves.label: Vampire Fiction
leaves.defn: A story whose central figures are vampires, as hunters, monsters or anti-heroes (Vampire Hunter D, Trinity Blood, Vanitas no Karte, Kizumonogatari). A vampire love story goes to C5-8.
leaves.see: C5-8 Paranormal Romance; C9 Horror Anime

subs.label: Magical Girl Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by what the heroine's magic is for: everyday wishes, battle, and the deconstruction of both

leaves.label: Majokko (Classic Magical Girl)
leaves.defn: A magical-girl series whose heroine uses magic, often with a transforming item and mascot, in everyday life rather than in battle (Mahoutsukai Sally, Mahou no Tenshi Creamy Mami, Cardcaptor Sakura, Ojamajo Doremi). Teams fighting monsters go to C4-2.
leaves.see: C4-2 Magical Girl Warrior; C11 Children's & Family Anime

leaves.label: Magical Girl Warrior
leaves.defn: A magical-girl series whose transformed heroines, usually a team, fight monsters or villains (Bishoujo Senshi Sailor Moon, Futari wa Precure, Mahou Shoujo Lyrical Nanoha, Senki Zesshou Symphogear). Grim deconstructions go to C4-3.
leaves.aliases: sentai magical girl, battle magical girl, magical boy
leaves.see: C4-1 Majokko; C4-3 Dark Magical Girl; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by audience and gender play: shōjo warrior teams, otaku-oriented battle magical girls, magical boys and parodies last

leaves.label: Dark Magical Girl
leaves.defn: A magical-girl series that deconstructs the form, making the contract, battles and transformation sources of trauma, death or despair (Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica, Yuuki Yuuna wa Yuusha de Aru, Mahou Shoujo Ikusei Keikaku, Mahou Shoujo Site).
leaves.see: C4-2 Magical Girl Warrior; C8 Drama, Mystery & Psychological Anime

subs.label: Romance Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the romantic engine: the girl's love story, comedy and harem forms, drama, then supernatural, fantasy and same-sex romance traditions

leaves.label: Shōjo Romance
leaves.defn: A love story told from a girl's point of view in the shōjo-manga tradition, about first love, confession and the couple's bond (Kimi ni Todoke, Ao Haru Ride, Marmalade Boy, Fruits Basket). Comedy-first school romance goes to C5-4; one heroine wooed by many to C5-3.
leaves.see: C5-2 Josei Romance; C5-3 Reverse Harem; C5-4 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by setting: school first love, comic and boy's-eye shōjo romance, period and adult shōjo romance

leaves.label: Josei Romance
leaves.defn: A love story about adult women's work, friendship and relationships, from the josei-manga tradition (Nana, Hachimitsu to Clover, Paradise Kiss, Wotaku ni Koi wa Muzukashii).
leaves.see: C5-1 Shōjo Romance; C5-6 Romantic Drama
leaves.axis: by tone: adult romantic drama, workplace comedy

leaves.label: Reverse Harem
leaves.defn: A romance in which one heroine is surrounded and courted by several young men (Ouran Koukou Host Club, Hana yori Dango, Uta no Prince-sama-type otome adaptations such as Kiniro no Corda, Diabolik Lovers).
leaves.see: C5-1 Shōjo Romance; C5-5 Harem; C3-3 Otome Isekai
leaves.axis: by source: shōjo-manga reverse harem, otome-game adaptations

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romance whose engine is comic: misunderstandings, pride, teasing and slow-burning confessions between one central couple (Toradora!, Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai, Karakai Jouzu no Takagi-san, Tonikaku Kawaii). A boy courted by many girls goes to C5-5; a girl's first-love story to C5-1.
leaves.see: C5-5 Harem; C5-1 Shōjo Romance; C10 Comedy Anime
leaves.axis: by the comic engine: school love comedy, teasing, otaku and gamer romance, marriage and cohabitation, workplace

leaves.label: Harem
leaves.defn: A romance in which one ordinary male lead is surrounded by several girls who desire him (Love Hina, Tenchi Muyou!, Nisekoi, 5-toubun no Hanayome). One girl courted by many men goes to C5-3.
leaves.see: C5-3 Reverse Harem; C5-4 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by what assembles the harem: domestic and school setting, dating-sim adaptation, sci-fi and fantasy arrivals

leaves.label: Romantic Drama
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is longing, loss, illness, love triangles or separation rather than comedy (Clannad, White Album 2, Byousoku 5 Centimeter, Koi wa Ameagari no You ni).
leaves.see: C5-4 Romantic Comedy; C5-7 Sekai-kei; C8 Drama, Mystery & Psychological Anime
leaves.axis: by source and age: visual-novel drama, school-age drama, adult drama, feature films

leaves.label: Sekai-kei
leaves.defn: A love story in which a teenage couple's relationship is tied directly to the fate of the world, with society in between left out (Saishuu Heiki Kanojo, Kimi no Na wa., Tenki no Ko, Seishun Buta Yarou).
leaves.see: C5-6 Romantic Drama; C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime

leaves.label: Paranormal Romance
leaves.defn: A love story between a human and a supernatural or artificial being: goddess, android, alien, yōkai, vampire or ghost (Aa! Megami-sama!, Chobits, Kamisama Hajimemashita, Vampire Knight). Supernatural stories without a romance engine go to C3.
leaves.see: C5-5 Harem; C3-13 Yōkai Fiction; C3-15 Vampire Fiction
leaves.axis: by the beloved's nature: goddess, android and alien; yōkai and monster; vampire; ghost

leaves.label: Romantic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A love story set in a fantasy or fairy-tale kingdom whose engine is the courtship (Akagami no Shirayuki-hime, Akatsuki no Yona, Unnamed Memory, Loop 7-kaime no Akuyaku Reijou). Rebirth into an otome game goes to C3-3.
leaves.aliases: fantasy romance, villainess romance, konyaku haki
leaves.see: C3-3 Otome Isekai; C3-5 High Fantasy
leaves.axis: by the romance plot: fairy-tale and court romance, villainess and broken-engagement romance

leaves.label: Boys' Love
leaves.defn: A romance between male characters in the boys' love (yaoi) tradition (Junjou Romantica, Given, Sasaki to Miyano, Loveless).
leaves.see: C5-11 Yuri; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by setting and mode: school and youth BL, adult and workplace BL, fantasy and OVA BL

leaves.label: Yuri
leaves.defn: A romance or intense bond between female characters in the yuri tradition (Maria-sama ga Miteru, Yagate Kimi ni Naru, Adachi to Shimamura, Citrus).
leaves.see: C5-10 Boys' Love; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by mode: everyday and school yuri, fantasy and comic yuri
